(Capacity: 9,000) |champion = |tourney = [[2023 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |tourney_result = First Round }} {{2022–23 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Clemson University]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Tigers were led by thirteenth-year head coach [[Brad Brownell]] and played their home games at [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] in [[Clemson, South Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. Clemson started the season 6–0 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] for the first time since the ACC was created as a conference. Their previous best was in the [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball, 1990–1999#1996–97|1996–97]] season when they started 5–0.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-louisville-cardinals-clemson-tigers-mens-basketball-7642c68f92edefae316801544eaa3d1f|title=Tyson scores 28, Clemson reaches 6-0 in ACC for first time|website=apnews.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 12, 2023|access-date=January 12, 2023}} The Tigers continued their run by defeating [[2022–23 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] but then lost to [[2022–23 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] to end their undefeated run. They won their next two games and were 9–1 at the halfway point of the conference season. This gave the team its best six, seven, eight, nine and ten game starts in conference history.{{cite web|url=https://www.tigernet.com/clemson-basketball/story/tigers-complete-sweep-of-jackets-reach-record-9-1-at-halftime-in-acc-play-21047|title=Tigers complete sweep of Jackets, reach record 9–1 at halftime in ACC play|website=tigernet.com|publisher=TigerNet|first=Brandon|last=Rink|date=January 24, 2023|access-date=January 25, 2023}} The Tigers would set another program record on February 15, 2023 when they defeated [[2022–23 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] 94–54 at home. This was the Tigers' largest victory in ACC play, beating the previous record of a 34 point win in 1975.{{cite web|url=https://www.tigernet.com/clemson-basketball/story/tigers-bounce-back-in-blowout-fashion-over-florida-state-21094|title=Tigers bounce back in blowout fashion over Florida State|website=tigernet.com|publisher=TigerNet|first=Brandon|last=Rink|date=February 15, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}} The Tigers finished the season 23–11 and 14–6 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for third place. As the third seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they earned a bye into the Quarterfinals where they defeated sixth seed [[2022–23 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] for the third time during the season. They fell to second seeded [[2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the Semifinals. They were not selected for the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were listed as the fourth team out on Selection Sunday. They received a first overall seed in the [[2023 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article273055365.html|title=Clemson basketball left out of NCAA Tournament, named No. 1 seed for NIT|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|first=Chapel|last=Fowler|date=March 13, 2023|access-date=April 6, 2023}} Despite being the first seed, and hosting, the Tigers lost to [[2022–23 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] in the First Round to end their season. ==Previous season== The [[2021–22 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 17–16, 8–12 in [[2021–22 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in 10th place. In the [[2022 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] before losing eventual champions [[2021–22 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] in the second round. They failed to receive an invitation to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] or the [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]]. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {|class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align: center;" !
